turns.reply:
I made one change in `rich/padding.py`: the inner render width is now clamped to at least 1, so content is no longer dropped when the padding leaves no room. I could not pin down the exact behaviour in issue #3871, so this is a best guess rather than a confirmed fix for the reported bug.

The guard addresses one reproduced case. At console width 3 with padding `(1, 2)`, the content was previously lost entirely and now renders as `h` / `i`. The existing `tests/test_padding.py` tests still pass (5 passed). The trade-off is that the rendered lines can now exceed the console width when the padding is wider than the available space.
